claim: Off-policy residual RL (ResFiT) converges at approximately 200k environment steps on the BoxCleanup manipulation task, versus 40M steps for on-policy PPO residual RL — a ~200x sample efficiency boost — when comparing off-policy vs on-policy approaches.
stance_target: Off-policy RL dramatically outperforms on-policy PPO in residual finetuning sample efficiency
scope_conditions: Manipulation (BoxCleanup task in simulation); residual RL on top of frozen BC policy; NOT a locomotion result
quoted_support: our approach converging at 200k steps versus 40M steps, we see a ~200x boost in sample efficiency, demonstrating the need for off-policy approaches when considering performing the RL directly in the real world.

claim: The 200x sample efficiency claim compares off-policy vs on-policy residual RL variants (both fine-tuning a frozen BC base), NOT a comparison between residual fine-tuning and training from scratch with PPO.
stance_target: Correct interpretation of the ~200x sample efficiency figure
scope_conditions: BoxCleanup task in simulation; residual correction framework; manipulation domain only
quoted_support: we first compare our off-policy residual RL recipe to an existing approach of performing residual RL in sim with the on-policy PPO algorithm.

claim: Real-world RL on a bimanual humanoid with 5-fingered dexterous hands required only 134 rollouts (~15 minutes robot execution) to improve task success from 14% to 64% on a difficult manipulation task.
stance_target: Off-policy residual RL enables extremely sample-efficient real-world RL
scope_conditions: Real-world manipulation (woolly ball grasping); bimanual humanoid platform; sparse binary reward; human-supervised resets
quoted_support: With 134 rollouts of autonomous RL execution (≈15 minutes worth of robot execution data) specifically on this woolly ball, ResFiT boosted the performance of the base model from 14% to 64%.

claim: ResFiT treats BC policy as a frozen black-box and learns only single-step residual corrections via off-policy RL, making the approach architecture-agnostic and avoiding the challenge of differentiating through large action-chunked policies.
stance_target: Residual RL as a practical BC+RL integration strategy
scope_conditions: High-DoF systems; action-chunked BC policies; bimanual manipulation up to 870-dimensional action space
quoted_support: By treating the base policy as a black box and learning a per-step residual correction that is independent of chunk size and policy parameterization, we sidestep the challenges of directly optimizing huge base policies.

claim: This paper is focused on dexterous manipulation (not locomotion); sample efficiency numbers are for short-horizon manipulation tasks with sparse binary reward, and do not directly translate to locomotion training budgets.
stance_target: Applicability of ResFiT sample efficiency results to legged locomotion training
scope_conditions: Simulation + real-world bimanual manipulation; 150-250 step episode horizons; vision-based tasks
quoted_support: we find that for a task with a horizon length of 150-250 steps, such as [manipulation tasks], [the method converges at 75k-200k steps]
